project.name: VI_Focused_Coding_Curricula
project.purpose: Publish four accessible introductory programming curricula (Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, and Java) as one mdBook on GitHub Pages, with an optional post-capstone Kotlin supplement for Java learners.

For the cross-platform command pass, the user explicitly requested all Markdown files; the only archived-folder changes were PowerShell equivalents immediately following existing Bash-family command blocks. Do not alter other archived content.

Preserve the established curriculum scope and learning progression. Make user-authorized modernization and expansion edits to active materials while retaining the original teaching intent, examples, and exercises where appropriate.
Record every implementation change in CHANGES.md.

Do not proceed until the previous step's commit succeeds and its SHA is recorded here.
If validation fails, record evidence, commit a checkpoint if possible, and stop. Never force-push or rewrite history.

Treat cs_curriculum_final/ as reference-only unless the user explicitly authorizes a defined exception. The 2026-10-30 cross-platform pass changed archived Markdown only to add immediately following PowerShell equivalents for existing Bash-family command examples.
For AI guidance, cover both instructor preparation and student use; require human verification, privacy protection, accessibility review, disclosure where required, and a non-AI route.

The version baseline last checked on 2026-10-30 is Python 3.12 minimum (examples remain 3.12-compatible), Node.js 26 LTS, TypeScript 7.0.2, JDK 25 LTS, and optional Kotlin 2.4.21. Recheck official release pages before future version upgrades.

TypeScript compiles to JavaScript; do not describe TypeScript source as directly executed by Node.js or as having automatic runtime validation. Keep strict compiler guidance and runtime validation at external-data boundaries.

Cross-platform documentation rule: every executable fenced bash, sh, shell, or zsh command block must be followed immediately by a functionally equivalent fenced powershell block labeled for Windows 11. Keep Bash-family examples first for macOS/Linux, use Windows-native commands (including winget where appropriate), and update both blocks together whenever commands change.

Environment management rule: Python projects must use uv for managed interpreters, project environments, and dependencies (uv init, uv add, uv run, uv sync, uv tree). Never recommend bare/global pip install or python -m pip install for course dependencies. JavaScript and TypeScript packages must be installed locally in the project with npm install or npm install --save-dev and run with npx/npm scripts; avoid global npm installs. Java projects should use Maven or Gradle wrappers. Do not recommend Volta.

Editor choice rule: list Theia IDE (https://theia-ide.org/#theiaide) as an alternative to VS Code for all relevant language setups. Verify language extension availability through Open VSX and test the learner's screen-reader workflow. JetBrains IDEs are intentionally not recommended for introductory learners because their extensive feature set adds unnecessary complexity.
